Founded in 2011, we offer our audience everything from breaking news to reviews to award-winning features and investigations, on our site, in video, and in podcasts. 2026-07-28T18:02:25+00:00 https://www.theverge.com/rss/index.xml https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/01/verge-rss-large_80b47e.png?w=150&h=150&crop=1 Sheena Vasani https://www.theverge.com/?p=971976 2026-07-28T13:53:51-04:00 2026-07-28T13:53:51-04:00 The Tile Pro offers the longest Bluetooth range of any Tile tracker. | Image: Tile Apple’s latest AirTag may seem like the obvious choice if you own an iPhone and are shopping for a Bluetooth tracker, but it’s not the most affordable option. For families that contain both Android and Apple devices, it might be better to pick up the latest Tile Pro instead. It works well across both platforms, and right now it’s on sale for $23.99 ($11 off) at Amazon and directly from Tile . This is its cheapest price in 2026 so far and only $1 shy of the all-time low we saw in October. Tile Pro Where to Buy: $34.99 $23.99 at Amazon $34.99 $23.99 at Tile As Tile’s most capable tracker, the Pro offers a Bluetooth range of up to 500 feet and the loudest ring of its lineup at 110 decibels, making it easier to locate misplaced items nearby. While it doesn’t tap into Apple’s Find My or Google’s Find Hub networks, its Life360 app remains a reliable option for keeping tabs on valuables both near and far.  The Tile Pro can also save you a little money in a few ways compared to Apple’s AirTag.  For starters, it includes a built-in keyring hole, so you can attach it to your keys, backpack, or luggage without buying a separate holder. On top of that, Tile includes a handful of free extras that Apple doesn’t provide, like two days of location history and Place Alerts that notify you when members of your Life360 Circle arrive at or leave certain places. If you’re willing to pay for a subscription (which starts at $7.99 a month) you’ll also gain access to features like SOS alerts that can connect you to emergency services, crash detection, roadside assistance, and even free towing depending upon the plan you choose. ]]> Brad Bourque https://www.theverge.com/?p=971634 2026-07-28T14:02:25-04:00 2026-07-28T13:48:03-04:00 While the summer months are great for putting in the miles on your favorite bike, it can be frustrating to have to hang it up when the weather turns. This smart bike trainer turns your road bike into an indoor exercise bike, with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to connect to your PC, iOS, or Android device, and support for a wide variety of interactive and training apps. Multiple retailers have the Kickr Core 2 on sale for $399.99 (usually $549.99) in both the Cog and Click version ( Wahoo , Amazon ) which fits 8-13 speed bikes, and the version with an included 11-speed cassette ( Wahoo , Amazon ). Wahoo Kickr Core 2 Where to Buy: $549.99 $399.99 at Wahoo (11-speed cassette) $549.99 $399.99 at Wahoo (Cog and Click) One of the main advantages to a trainer like the Kickr is access to dynamically adjustable resistance, which can work in concert with training apps to tune your workout, or interact with riding apps to replicate inclines and group rides. If you use heart rate or cadence trackers, the Kickr Core 2 can connect directly to them with ANT+ support, and the Cog and Click version includes controllers for changing your virtual gears that hook to your handlebars. I use mine to keep pedaling during the winter months in the Pacific Northwest, joining other cyclists from all over the world for group rides, challenges, and races using Zwift . Other deals to consider The Razer BlackShark V2 Pro is on sale at Amazon for $76.18, within a dollar of its all-time low price. This gaming headset has features designed for competitive gamers, including sound isolating ear cups to keep you focused, a wideband microphone so your teammates hear your callouts clearly, and a low-latency 2.4GHz connection. They’re compatible with PlayStation 4 and 5, PC, and mobile devices. Costco members can grab the Dell Ultra Sharp 32-inch 6K monitor for $799.99, a $200 break from the usual price. While the 60Hz refresh and IPS panel aren’t exactly cutting-edge, the screen makes up for it with a super dense 6144 x 3456 resolution, where it has few direct competitors. This screen would be a great fit for an office setup, with a built-in webcam for taking meetings and KVM support for switching between multiple systems quickly. For connectivity, it supports HDMI and Mini DisplayPort at 6K, Thunderbolt 4, and 2.5GbE Ethernet. Paper Mario: The Thousand Year Door for the Nintendo Switch 2 is on sale for $31.99 at Woot , almost half off the usual price of $59.99. This classic Gamecube game has been remastered for newer consoles, and sees you guiding a 2D version of Mario through a turn-based RPG where you’ll upgrade your abilities, solve puzzles, and fight a variety of enemies. It has a unique art style and gameplay elements you won’t find in other non-paper Mario games. ]]> Jay Peters https://www.theverge.com/?p=971880 2026-07-28T11:59:37-04:00 2026-07-28T11:59:37-04:00 Warner Bros.
